angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 639,348 km at 96.02 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.4148 +/- 0.0104 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 96.02 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.919 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-93 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 639,348 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.911 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-93 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5669 +/- 75 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-93 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-93 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-93.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.471, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, BD+38 3583: main object type Er*, Eruptive Variable
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-93 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.18 dex, from Marcy et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-93 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.10565, from Gajdoš et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019RAA....19...41G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-93 (pscomppars): age 5.05 Gyr, from Marcy et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/678/A24/tablec1 (New rotation periods of 67163 Kepler stars), column ProtACF: 29.41 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 16 catalogued periods, 10 of them within 20% of it
